identity: Surgeon and university teacher · United Kingdom · 1827–1912
title: Joseph Lister's birth chart
metaDescription: Joseph Lister's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.9° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 14.9° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 14.9° Aries. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 15.5° Aries; Venus stands at 0.8° Pisces; Mars stands at 12.8° Taurus. The tradition reads a mind that decides at speaking speed from Mercury, taste tuned to mood and undertow from Venus, drive that grinds rather than flares from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Venus trine Saturn, 0.5° of separation. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Mercury at 0.5°, and Mercury square Neptune at 0.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aries at 14.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Pisces at 0.8° is in exaltation; Mars in Taurus at 12.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Cancer at 0.3° is in detriment. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 fire, 3 earth, 2 water, 1 air by element and 7 cardinal, 1 mutable, 1 fixed by mode. Mercury and Jupiter were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.2° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
